field: Positioning / competitive strategy (Typefully, Hypefury, Taplio, Buffer, Black Magic, Tweet Hunter, Postwise)

arc-b.verdict: The only page that turns the wedge into a noun. 'Receipts' is a category of one, and next to it every competitor's homepage looks like it's hiding something.
arc-b.loved: The till receipt: MOVE / WHY / CUT / KEPT / WORDS 17→10. It proves 'your facts stay' line by line ('KEPT: sizing down · after a loss'), and 'receipts' already means proof on X. It runs through the nav, the hero, the section titles and even the never-list ('WILL IT EVER, ON ITS OWN… NEVER'), so the device carries the positioning. No tool in the category shows its work. The 'Try yours' tab is honest too: it flags soft words live and says the rewrite runs in the app instead of faking one.
problems: 'STILL SOUNDS LIKE YOU: YES' is the product grading itself. It's the one unverifiable line on a page built on itemized proof.
'Start free. Pay when it works.' brings in an outcome promise that the X section then says nobody can make.

The receipt, the money shot, gets cropped by the 900px fold on desktop. Five annotations compete for the first screen (wavy-line note, receipt note, two stickers, Real/Try tabs), so the wedge is all there but fighting itself.
Rebrand risk for the beachhead: warm paper, lime and heavy grotesk say 'creator/newsletter tool' more than 'trader tool'. The examples carry the crypto niche and the look doesn't.
arc-b.fix: Lift the full receipt into the resting first screen at 1440×900 (trim the proof card, fold the 'Every rewrite prints a receipt' note into the receipt) and replace 'STILL SOUNDS LIKE YOU: YES' with something checkable like 'KEPT: your lowercase'.

typefully-a.verdict: The sharpest copy in the set ('Make it hookworthy.' makes the brand the standard), wearing the category's most familiar clothes.
typefully-a.loved: Two strategic moves no other design made. The brand name becomes the adjective for a good opener ('They read one line. Make it hookworthy.'). And pricing leads with 'Sharpening is free. Forever.', which turns the wedge into a free acquisition weapon against every competitor's paid AI tier. The playground is honest as well: type your own line, the soft words get flagged, and it says the rewrite runs in the app.
problems: Visually it's the category default: dark UI with a draft card beside an X preview. That's the layout Typefully made famous and Tweet Hunter and Black Magic reuse, and the sticky Previews/Week/Inbox/Results index brings back the incumbent feature tour, so a skimmer files it as 'another Typefully'.
The receipt (Kept/Cut) sits below the 900px fold. At rest the first screen shows only draft → post, which every AI composer shows.

'Sharpening is free. Forever.' sits right beside 'Claude rewrites 20/month' with nothing on how they differ. A competitor or a Reddit thread will call it bait unless the page says what a free Sharpen includes.
Invented body copy under example posts ('Year one I overtraded…') blurs 'your facts stay': it's unclear whether the tool added it.
typefully-a.fix: Shrink the hero stack so the receipt ('Led with the number · Kept: $10k · 3 years · Cut: just wanted to share · lol') is visible at rest at 1440×900. It's the one thing in this hero Typefully can't show.

arc-a.verdict: Owns the first line for one screen, then quietly goes back to being a dark AI scheduler.
arc-a.loved: The peel: soft words come off as stickers into a 'Peeled off' tray with 'Stick them back on'. Nobody in the category has a mechanic like it, and it shows 'your facts stay' without saying it, because everything left behind is your words.
problems: The receipt, the real moat, only slides out after the animation and sits under the card at the fold. At rest the hero says 'it rewrites', which Typefully, Tweet Hunter, Taplio and Postwise all say.
Below the hero it's the standard dark-SaaS feature tour (rounded tiles, photo strip, highlighted middle price card). Next to Tweet Hunter or Black Magic it's indistinguishable from section 3 on.
No way to try your own line ('See real rewrites' jumps to presets), so the only stand-in for missing testimonials is four curated examples.
'Start free. Pay when it works.' hints at results, right on a page that says 'Nobody can promise reach.'
arc-a.fix: Make the receipt part of the resting hero (MOVE · KEPT · CUT under the sharpened line, not only after the peel) and add a type-your-own input that underlines soft words live.

awwwards-b.verdict: A beautiful category of one, but the category is 'editor', which puts it next to Grammarly and Hemingway, not ahead of Typefully.
awwwards-b.loved: The galley proof with real proofreader's marks and margin notes ('warm-up, hedge' → 'Led with the question.') is the most convincing picture of 'shows its work' in the set. 'Your facts stay. The fluff goes.' is the clearest wedge headline on any of the five pages.
problems: 'Write it rough. Post it sharp.' never says 'first line'. Any AI writing assistant could print it, so the first-line category claim drops down to the lede.

A self-own in the 11 PM story: the voice note says 'after a loss you size down. that's the post.' and the 'DRAFTED · IN YOUR VOICE' card adds 'so i think … honestly just'. The drafting feature visibly adds the soft words Sharpen exists to remove.

Galley proofs, Garamond and a 2B pencil speak to newsletter and literary writers. Crypto traders, the stated beachhead, get the least native page of the five, and the X-pays moment reads as an aside instead of urgency.
No try-your-own. The hero cycles four presets, so every bit of proof is curated.
awwwards-b.fix: Put the first line in the H1. Keep 'Write it rough.' and make the second line about the opener, so the page claims the first-line category and not 'writing'.

apple-b.verdict: Sells the outcome in the feed so well that it reads like every 'write viral posts' tool. The receipt, the actual moat, is missing from the hero.
apple-b.loved: The drifting feed of soft openers ('hot take but i kind of think', 'not to brag but', from handles like onchain otto and deltaneutral) names the enemy at a glance. It's the most crypto-native framing in the set.
problems: 'Write the line they stop for' is an outcome promise in growth-tool grammar (stop-the-scroll is Tweet Hunter, Postwise and Hypefury territory), and Inter on a big blue field looks like Taplio or Tweet Hunter. The category of one becomes 'AI writer for X'.

No wedge above the fold: no receipt and no 'your facts stay'. The hero card shows invented body copy ('I lost $4,000 in March…') the engine never wrote, so it's selling a whole post, not a first line.

'Posts get paid.' overstates the change (only accounts past Premium/500/500K get paid), and the giant Premium/500/500K tiles look like Hookworthy's own stats at a glance, which is exactly the invented-proof look a skeptic is scanning for.
'Try a line' opens four presets you can't type into, and Pro/Studio show 'Billed yearly' without the $16/$24 monthly prices until you toggle. Small credibility leaks on a page with no other proof.
apple-b.fix: Swap the invented body copy on the hero post for its receipt ('Made it a question · Kept: sizing down, after a loss · 17→10 words') so the mechanism, not the outcome, is what you see first.

pickWhy: It's the only design where the whole wedge (Sharpen, receipt, facts kept, nothing posts without you) sits in the first screen, and it makes 'receipts', which already means proof on X, the brand's own noun. That's how it gets credibility without logos or testimonials. It's also the one competitors can't answer with a release: Typefully can ship a hook-rewrite button in a sprint, but not a brand built on showing its work.
combo: Ship arc-b's receipt system and honest 'Try yours', but take typefully-a's words: test 'They read one line. Make it hookworthy.' as the H1 and use 'Sharpening is free. Forever.' (with a one-line note on what free Sharpen covers vs. Claude rewrites) as the pricing headline. Use apple-b's crypto-handle feed of soft openers as the 'before' backdrop for traders, and add one quiet line near the hero, 'Since Sept 8, X pays for original posts, not replies', which none of the five heroes say.
